items.stem: In QuickBooks Online, which document should be used when a customer pays at the moment of sale with no invoice outstanding?

options.rationale: Correct: a sales receipt records an immediate paid sale.
An invoice is for amounts to be paid later.
A bill records money the business owes a vendor.
A purchase order requests goods; it is not a sale record.

items.explanation: Correct: a sales receipt records an immediate paid sale.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which two statements about bank reconciliation in QuickBooks Online are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It compares recorded transactions against the bank statement
options.rationale: Correct: reconciliation matches the books to the bank.

options.text: It should end with a zero difference before completing
options.rationale: Correct: an unexplained difference means it is not reconciled.

options.text: It automatically creates the company's chart of accounts
options.rationale: Reconciliation does not build the chart of accounts.

options.text: It is only needed once when the company is created
options.rationale: Reconciliation is a recurring task, not one-off.

items.explanation: Correct: reconciliation matches the books to the bank.

items.stem: Entering both a 'bill' and an 'expense' for the very same purchase will most likely cause:

options.text: The cost to be recorded twice (double counting)
options.rationale: Correct: recording both duplicates the expense.

options.text: The cost to be omitted entirely
options.rationale: The problem is duplication, not omission.
It does not auto-reconcile; it creates an error.

items.explanation: Correct: recording both duplicates the expense.
